facts.claim: The only implementation of the real read is PlatformFileSystemBase.ReadLinkTarget. It returns Factory.GetFileInfo(path).LinkTarget ?? Factory.GetDirectoryInfo(path).LinkTarget. It wraps that in catch (IOException) and catch (UnauthorizedAccessException), and both blocks return null. IsLinkTarget is defined as ReadLinkTarget(linkPath) is not null, so it reports false for a link it cannot read.

facts.claim: PathCanonicalizer.Resolve treats null as 'not a link' and returns the candidate as the final path. That is the wrong-answer path: an unreadable link stops resolution at the link itself. If the read raised, the exception would escape Resolve and Canonicalize (no try/catch anywhere in the file). The file already throws IOException for a symlink cycle at the link-depth ceiling, so an IOException from Canonicalize is existing precedent.

facts.claim: PathCanonicalizer.Canonicalize returns CanonicalPath, not Verdict. The contract's wording for this call site is 'it returns a denial carrying the reason, through Verdict.Deny'. That cannot be done at this method without a signature change. The exception would have to be caught at the callers of Canonicalize.

facts.claim: SymlinkOps.EnsurePointsTo reads the link and compares it ordinally with the wanted target. Null is not equal, so it calls MakeLinkTarget, which re-points the link. Today an unreadable link is therefore overwritten (or MakeLinkTarget fails). If the read raised, the exception would propagate from EnsurePointsTo. Its only caller is CreationHelper.RepairLink, which catches only UnauthorizedAccessException and turns it into RepairOutcome.NotRepairable(exception.Message). An IOException from the read would be uncaught there; an UnauthorizedAccessException would be caught.
facts.evidence: src/AgentGuard.Engine/Setup/SymlinkOps.cs:40-46; src/AgentGuard.Engine/Setup/CreationHelper.cs:235-243 (single call site, found by grep EnsurePointsTo).

facts.claim: BinSymlinkCondition and CurrentSymlinkCondition each read the link and pass the result to string.Equals(actual, expected). Null is not equal, so they return ConditionState.Broken with the message "... points at '', expected '...'", and an unreadable link is reported as a link pointing at nothing. Neither has a catch. Both sit in DetectInstalled, which MachineCondition.cs:26 calls. Whether MachineCondition or any condition runner catches IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException was not read, so what a raised read would do above these two methods is unproven.

At the catch the JsonException/FormatException/IOException object (message, path = `file` argument) is in scope; for invalid-signature and expired the cause is known by branch but not recorded. facts.claim: GrantStore's public result type cannot carry a reason: IGrantStore.GetActiveGrantsAsync returns Task<IReadOnlyList<Grant>> only (a flat list of good grants). GetActiveGrantsAsync also returns an empty list silently when _publicKey.IsEmpty or the grant directory does not exist, so 'no key', 'bad key length' (Create swallows a wrong-length key to Empty at GrantStore.Create) and 'no directory' are indistinguishable from 'no grants'. The only Verdict producers downstream are FileGuard.PrecheckWriteAsync (FileGuard.cs:358 'requires an authorizing grant') and ReconcileAsync (FileGuard.cs:236, drift reasons via DriftReason), which call GetActiveGrantsAsync at FileGuard.cs:236 and :355 and never see why grants were dropped.

facts.claim: WindowsUserPresence catches at lines 154 (IsHelloAvailableAsync, returns false) and 175 (TryVerifyWithHelloAsync, returns null) are `catch (Exception)` with no variable, both under signed-off CA1031 SuppressMessage. The methods return bool and WindowsPresenceResult? (internal enum Verified/Cancelled/NoMethod/Failed) respectively; neither can carry text, and Verdict is not reachable: presence uses PresenceResult(ApprovalReason Reason, string Detail), not Verdict. The exception message IS available at the catch. The reachable carrier is PresenceResult.Detail: WindowsPresenceCheck.Check builds it as $"Windows user presence -> {result} -> {reason}" from a bare enum, so the cause would have to travel from WindowsUserPresence.VerifyAsync (returns Task<WindowsPresenceResult>, internal interface IWindowsUserPresence) to WindowsPresenceCheck. Note line 154's fail-closed result is NoMethod (headless fast fail), and 175's null falls through to the credential prompt, so 175 is not a denial at all but a fallback.
facts.evidence: src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Windows/Presence/WindowsUserPresence.cs:78-92,143-178; WindowsPresenceCheck.cs:29-37,55-61; PresenceResult.cs:13; WindowsPresenceResult.cs:10-22

facts.claim: BuildOutputSkipRule.ShouldSkip (BuildOutputSkipRule.cs:27-56) catches IOException (line 47) and UnauthorizedAccessException (line 51) and returns false, meaning 'do not skip, descend'. Verdict is not reachable: a bool-returning predicate inside a scanner that returns IReadOnlyList<CanonicalPath>. The directory failure here is not a denial; it makes the scan walk into the bin/obj directory. The exception object is in scope. If it were allowed to propagate instead, ScanAsync's callers already convert exceptions into reasoned outcomes: FileGuard Post via TryReadCurrentAsync/Deny (FileGuard.cs:125-129) and Pre capture via CaptureFailed($"...{exception.Message}") (FileGuard.cs ~195-225), though that capture catch is typed to IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException.

facts.claim: In PrivilegedWriter no Verdict exists at the swallow point, so a warn is not reachable there as written. IPrivilegedWriter.ExecuteAsync returns plain Task and takes only (IReadOnlyList<Effect>, CancellationToken). Its sole caller, Pipeline.RunPostAsync line 157, calls it before aggregating the verdicts. A warn is reachable only by changing the return type (a new result type, which the contract forbids) or by throwing out of the writer and letting RunPostAsync's catch-all turn it into Verdict.Deny. That would change a deny-stands/best-effort behavior and would stop the remaining effects after a failed one. The contract's wording 'Verdict.Warn where a verdict is being produced, and otherwise report it to the caller' fits PrivilegedWriter as 'report it to the caller', but the mechanism is not settled by the contract.

The try has already executed 'return VerdictAggregator.Aggregate(verdicts)' (line 158) or 'return Verdict.Deny(...)' (line 166), so the verdict is already computed and a finally cannot change the returned value without restructuring (e.g. capture the verdict in a local, run the delete after it, and fold a Warn into it).
